messages:
Aisha (Support): Hey team — customer (Tom) hit a pretty confusing embeddings error after migrating projects. They see a dimension mismatch when decoding vectors. Error: \"InvalidEmbeddingDimension: expected 512, got 1536\". Looking for quick repro + root cause.

Tom (Customer): repro steps I used:
1) curl POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer ORG_KEY_abc' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"input": ["foo","bar"], "model":"auto"}'
2) server returns 400 with that dimension error. We used to get 512-dim vectors. Nothing in our code changed.

Jules (ML Eng): Thanks Tom. Two quick hypotheses: either the request routed to a different embedding model (one that returns 1536 dims) OR the project default changed. Can you paste the raw response headers & the small request_id from the error? Also did you include any x-project-id or x-org headers?

Tom (Customer): Here's the error payload and headers (scrubbed):
{
  "error": "InvalidEmbeddingDimension",
  "expected": 512,
  "received": 1536,
  "model": "text-embedding-ada-002",
  "request_id": "rq_01GGY..."
}
Response headers: x-request-id: rq_01GGY..., server: redwood-inference

Aisha (Support): Noted — model name in error is text-embedding-ada-002 (1536d). Customer says they expect redwood-embed-512. Tom, do you have multiple API keys? org-scoped vs project-scoped?

Tom (Customer): Yes — we have an org-level key (used by infra scripts) and per-project keys for apps. Our deploy automation sets Authorization: Bearer <ORG_KEY> on some calls. But our app uses project key. In this case the call was coming from our infra proxy which uses ORG_KEY (we thought routing would use project when x-project-id present).

Jules (ML Eng): That fits a known routing subtlety: when an org-scoped API key is used the platform uses the org's default model mapping (which for older orgs is still mapped to text-embedding-ada-002). Project defaults only apply if the request is authenticated with a project-scoped key or if a model param is explicitly supplied. If your infra proxy sets the org key and also sends x-project-id, we currently prioritize the Authorization context for model selection.

Aisha (Support): Repro guide for internal triage:
- Use ORG_KEY in Authorization with a project id header -> server routes to org default model
- Use PROJECT_KEY in Authorization -> server routes to project default model

Concrete curl repro that reproduces the bad path:
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer ORG_KEY_abc" -H "x-project-id: proj-123" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":["a","b"], "model":"auto"}'
```
This returns model: text-embedding-ada-002 -> 1536 dims.

Jules (ML Eng): Temporary mitigation for the customer:
- Best immediate fix: explicitly pass model=redwood-embed-512 in the request body/param to force correct model.
- Alternate: rotate to using the project-scoped API key in the Authorization header (recommended for prod apps).

Tom (Customer): Passing model param worked in our quick test: we got 512-d vectors back. But we need to scale and still want our infra proxy to call on behalf of projects without changing a million deployments.

Leo (SRE): Filed infra ticket INF-4521. Short-term options for us to support proxying without forcing key rotation:
1) Make the proxy include a header we check for model routing (e.g., x-project-api-key) — quick hack but security implications.
2) Adjust routing priority so explicit x-project-id + valid project membership overrides org default when present. This requires careful auth checks.

infra-bot: Assigned INF-4521 to Leo. ETA: triage today, fix in 48-72h if low risk.

Jules (ML Eng): Also calling out batching/throughput interactions we saw in similar cases: when batched requests combine inputs expecting 512 dims but backend used 1536-d model, we hit aggregator-level validation errors which cascade as 400s. If customer relies on batching at size 32+, advise validation on client side to ensure model param is set per request.

Aisha (Support): Action items:
- Tom: for now pass model=\"redwood-embed-512\" in request body or switch proxy to use project key (your choice). (owner: Tom)
- Leo/Jules: infra change to allow x-project-id to override org default if the project key relationship is provably correct (owner: Leo). INF-4521.
- Jules: follow-up doc blurb for devex to clarify auth vs routing model selection and recommended patterns (owner: Jules).

Tom (Customer): Thanks — we'll flip model param for now and wait for infra fix. Appreciate fast turnaround.

Aisha (Support): Marking resolved for support, will reopen if customer sees additional errors after infra patch. :thumbsup:
notes: Escalation about org vs project key causing wrong embedding model selection, leading to dimension mismatch errors. Includes repro curl, error payload, mitigation, and infra ticket reference.
